title: Life & Mana Recovery: Leech, Regeneration, Recoup, Recharge, and Flasks in Path of Exile 2
summary: How the five recovery methods in Path of Exile 2 actually work: Leech, Regeneration, Recoup, Energy Shield Recharge, and Flasks — what triggers each, which resource they fill, and how the 0.5 Leech rework changed everything.
description: A mechanic guide to Path of Exile 2 life and mana recovery: Leech rules and the 0.5 damage cap, Regeneration rates, Recoup as delayed recovery, Energy Shield Recharge start and interruption, and Flask burst sustain, with a comparison table and a choose-your-recovery diagnostic.
imageAlt: A Path of Exile 2 charm icon representing life and mana recovery methods
prerequisites: A basic understanding of Life, Mana, and Energy Shield as your character's resources
Familiarity with the character panel, buff icons, and reading item modifiers
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: Leech
body: Recovers a fraction of the damage you deal as Life, Mana, or Energy Shield — but only for the Damage Type and Hit type the leech modifier names. Most leech is physical Attack leech, so it does nothing on a fully elementally-converted build.

items.title: Regeneration
body: Continuous, always-on recovery of a resource over time. Not tied to hitting or being hit, and not stopped when the resource is full. Life and Energy Shield have no base regen; Mana regenerates on its own.

items.title: Recoup
body: Pays back a portion of the damage you take from a Hit as Life, Mana, or Energy Shield over a duration. It is delayed recovery, separate from Regeneration, and keeps running even at full resource.

items.title: Recharge
body: Energy Shield only. After you avoid damage for a short moment, your ES refills; any damaging hit interrupts it. The 0.5 update slowed recharge-start passives.

items.title: Flasks
body: Instant on-use burst of Life or Mana. The most reliable sustain when you cannot land hits (so Leech is weak) or take few hits (so Recoup is weak), limited by flask charges.

sections.title: Leech
paragraphs: Leech recovers a portion of the damage you deal as Life, Mana, or Energy Shield. The critical rule in Path of Exile 2 is that leech only applies to the Damage Type and Hit type named by the leech modifier. Most leech found on items grants physical Attack leech, which only counts physical damage dealt by attacks. A hit that deals none of the matching damage type leeches nothing at all.

The 0.5 update reworked Leech. Only one Leech instance can be active per resource at a time — if several trigger, only the one with the highest recovery rate applies and the others are ignored. There is also a damage cap: a single hit is treated as dealing at most 40,000 damage for Leech calculations, so very large hits no longer scale Leech without limit. The exact per-instance recovery rate and duration are client-version dependent; confirm precise coefficients in-game.
bullets: Leech requires you to deal a hit of the matching Damage Type — it is not 'any damage'.
Physical Attack Leech fails on a build that fully converts its physical damage to elemental.
One instance per resource (0.5): the highest recovery-rate instance wins.
40,000 damage cap per hit for Leech purposes (0.5).
Leech normally ends when the resource is full, so you must keep hitting to keep leeching.

sections.title: Regeneration
paragraphs: Regeneration is continuous, always-on recovery of a resource over time. It is not tied to dealing or taking damage. Life and Energy Shield have no base regeneration by default; Mana has a small base regeneration (about 4% of maximum Mana per second). All other regeneration comes from passive nodes, gear, or auras.

Regeneration can be a flat amount per second or a percentage of the resource's maximum. It is not stopped when the resource is full, and it is a separate mechanic from Leech, Recoup, and Recharge — modifiers to Regeneration do not affect those other recovery types.
bullets: Life and Energy Shield: no base regeneration; must be gained from modifiers.
Mana: base regeneration of roughly 4% of maximum Mana per second.
Flat regeneration and percent regeneration add to the base differently but both contribute.
Regeneration is continuous and works during boss immunity phases — excellent for sustained bossing.
Recovery Rate modifiers also multiply regeneration alongside other recovery types.

sections.title: Recoup
paragraphs: Recoup recovers a portion of the damage you take from a Hit, returned as Life, Mana, or Energy Shield over a duration (8 seconds by default in current Path of Exile 2). Each hit you take creates its own Recoup instance, and there is no cap on how many instances can run at once.

Recoup is NOT Regeneration and is not affected by modifiers to Regeneration. Unlike Leech, Recoup continues even when the resource is already full, though any excess is wasted. Damage over Time does not trigger Recoup. The exact base duration is client-version dependent (some community pages still cite older 4-second values); confirm precise numbers in-game.
bullets: Triggered by taking a Hit, not by dealing one.
Paid back over time (8 seconds base) — delayed recovery, not instant.
Distinct from Regeneration; uses its own modifier pool.
Damage over Time effects do not activate Recoup.
Per-hit instances are independent and uncapped in number.

sections.title: Recharge
paragraphs: Recharge applies to Energy Shield only. After you stop taking damage for a short period, your Energy Shield begins to refill at a rate based on your maximum Energy Shield. Any hit that deals damage interrupts recharge and resets the start delay.

In the 0.5 update, passive-tree recharge-start thresholds were reduced (for example the Mystic Stance node dropped from 30% to 12%), so Energy Shield generally starts recharging more slowly after a hit than before. Treat the exact node values as client-version dependent.
bullets: Energy Shield only — Life and Mana do not recharge.
Starts after a delay during which you take no damage.
Interrupted by any damaging hit.
0.5 nerfed recharge-start passives, so recovery after hits is slower.
Pairs best with high avoidance so you can stop getting hit.

sections.title: Flasks
paragraphs: Flasks provide an instant burst of Life or Mana recovery (or other effects) when used. They refill their charges from kills and, for some flask types, over time. Flasks are the most reliable burst sustain because they do not depend on hitting or being hit.

In boss fights where you cannot always land hits (so Leech is weak) and where you take few hits (so Recoup is weak), flask charges become your main planned sustain. Do not quote fixed flask sustain numbers without testing — values depend on flask tier, modifiers, and charge gain, which are client-version dependent.
bullets: Instant, on-use recovery of Life or Mana.
Charges come mainly from kills; some flasks refill over time.
Best burst sustain when Leech and Recoup are unreliable.
Boss sustain depends on charge income, not a fixed figure.
Flask recovery is separate from Regeneration.

sections.title: Choose your recovery
sections.intro: Pick the profile that matches your build. The tool points to the recovery methods that fit best.

rules.title: Attack build recovery
steps: Use physical Attack Leech if your hits deal physical damage.
If you convert physical to elemental, switch to a matching leech or use Recoup/Flask instead.
Keep a Life Flask for burst and consider small Regeneration for steady sustain.

rules.title: Caster build recovery
steps: Add Mana Leech or Mana Regeneration so spell costs do not drain you.
Use spell-damage leech only if your leech modifier supports spells.
Keep a Mana Flask and some Life recovery for survivability.

rules.title: Energy Shield build recovery
steps: Rely on Energy Shield Recharge after avoiding damage.
ES Leech is possible but recharge is steadier; note 0.5 slowed recharge-start.
Improve avoidance so recharge is not interrupted.

rules.title: Damage-over-Time build recovery
steps: Leech is weak because DoT is not a Hit — do not depend on it.
Use Recoup (you still take hits) plus Regeneration for stable sustain.
Keep Flasks for burst when Recoup lag is dangerous.

rules.title: Bossing-heavy build recovery
steps: Prioritize Regeneration and Flasks — both work during immunity phases.
Do not rely on Leech when you cannot land hits.
Use Recoup if the fight keeps dealing contact damage to you.

defaultResult.title: General recovery guidance
steps: Stack at least two independent recovery layers rather than one.
Match leech to your actual Damage Type and Hit type.
Keep Flasks as your reliable burst backstop in every fight.

sections.title: Worked examples
sections.caption: Three illustrative cases showing how Damage Type, Hit type, and resource shape the right recovery choice. No fixed numbers are promised.

cells.setup: Attack build converts 100% of physical damage to fire
cells.result: Physical Attack Leech leeches nothing — conversion removed the matching damage type. Use fire/chaos leech, Recoup, or Flasks instead.

cells.setup: Poison or ignite caster that lands few direct hits
cells.result: Leech is weak because DoT is not a Hit. Use Recoup (you still take hits) plus Regeneration for stable sustain.

cells.setup: ES build with high avoidance and some recharge-start investment
cells.result: Use ES Recharge after avoiding hits. ES Leech is possible but recharge is steadier; the 0.5 recharge-start nerfs slow the refill after a hit.

sections.note: These are teaching examples; exact sustain depends on your modifiers and client version.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Most recovery problems come from mismatched Damage Types or misunderstanding which mechanic triggers which layer, not from bad luck. Watch for these before you re-roll gear.
bullets: Have Leech but see no recovery: your damage type does not match the leech modifier (for example physical leech on a fully converted build).
Unstable Mana: no Mana Leech or Mana Regeneration, so skill costs drain you. Add mana leech, mana regen, or flasks.
Recharge never starts: you are taking constant damage. Improve avoidance or use another layer.
Thinking Recoup is Regeneration (or vice versa) — they use separate modifiers.
Expecting Leech to work during boss immunity phases when you cannot land hits.
Assuming Leech scales with huge hits after 0.5 — there is a 40,000 damage cap per hit.

sections.title: Common points of confusion
sections.intro: Paraphrased confusions players frequently raise about recovery mechanics.

cards.title: Physical leech on a converted build
body: A player converts all physical damage to fire and wonders why their physical Attack Leech heals nothing. The matching damage type is gone, so leech has nothing to count.

cards.title: Leech not working in a boss fight
body: During an immunity or untargetable phase the player cannot land hits, so no leech triggers. Regeneration and Flasks keep them alive instead.

cards.title: Recoup versus regeneration
body: A player stacks regeneration modifiers expecting Recoup to grow. They are separate pools; regeneration mods do not raise Recoup.

cards.title: Recharge keeps interrupting
body: An Energy Shield player stands in damage and recharge never completes. Any hit resets the start delay; avoidance is what lets ES refill.

entries.label: How To Leech In Path of Exile 2 | Is Leech Working?
entries.creator: HumbleHazard
entries.description: A community walkthrough of how Leech works in Path of Exile 2, the requirements for it to trigger, leech resistance, and how conversion interacts with leech after the 0.5 changes.
entries.takeaway: Leech only counts the damage type and hit type your leech modifier specifies, and the 0.5 rework capped per-hit leech and limited one instance per resource.

items.question: Does Leech work on any damage?
answer: No. Leech only applies to the Damage Type and Hit type named by the leech modifier. Common physical Attack leech only counts physical damage from attacks, so elemental or spell damage may leech nothing.

items.question: Why does my physical leech do nothing on my fire build?
answer: If your build converts 100% of physical damage to fire, there is no physical damage left for physical Attack Leech to count. Use a leech modifier that matches your actual damage type, or switch to Recoup or Flasks.

items.question: Is Recoup the same as Regeneration?
answer: No. Recoup pays back a portion of damage you take from hits over a duration, and it is a separate mechanic with its own modifiers. Regeneration is continuous recovery not tied to taking damage, and modifiers to one do not affect the other.

items.question: Why will my Energy Shield not recharge?
answer: Recharge only starts after you avoid damage for a short moment, and any damaging hit interrupts it. The 0.5 update also reduced recharge-start passives, so it begins more slowly. Improve avoidance so the delay can elapse.

items.question: Can one huge hit refill my whole life bar through Leech?
answer: Not after the 0.5 rework. A single hit is treated as dealing at most 40,000 damage for Leech calculations, so beyond that point bigger hits do not increase leech. Higher leech percentage still helps, but the per-hit cap stays.

items.question: Does Flask recovery count as Regeneration?
answer: No. Flasks are an instant on-use burst and are a separate recovery source. Recovery Rate modifiers may multiply flask recovery alongside other types, but flasks are not Regeneration.
